## TL;DR

Human-assigned tasks now get a standard `## Step-by-step guide` section in scaffolds and split-offs, shared validation warns (never blocks) when that heading is missing, and the task drawer surfaces the same message. PM and engineer built-in prompts were updated so agents file complete guides when splitting human work. Tests cover warnings, scaffolds, and split templates; `user-docs/cli.md` and `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md` document the contract. Scoped `repoos check` against `main` passed on resume after a prior turn timed out before handoff.

## Work and rationale

The failure mode was practical: held human tasks (keystore creation, provider sign-up, device checks) often shipped as two-line acceptance criteria, forcing the human to reverse-engineer steps after the fact. RepoOS already had strong contracts for AI task bodies (`## Problem`, `## Desired UX`, etc.) but nothing comparable for the one audience least able to fill gaps.

The fix is deliberately soft enforcement plus hard scaffolding. **Code** emits an immediate, named warning when `assigned_to: human` and the body lacks a `## Step-by-step guide` heading line; **prompts** tell the PM and engineer agents what belongs in that section; **templates** pre-create the heading so authors start in the right shape.

Central logic lives in `humanTaskGuideWarning()` in `src/core/task-underspecified.ts`. It returns `null` for non-human assignees or when a step-by-step heading line is present (including the empty scaffold placeholder under that heading). Otherwise it returns a single canonical string naming the missing section and summarizing expected content (numbered steps, commands or click paths, secret handling, success checks, report-back). One function feeds CLI `repoos new` / `repoos update`, HTTP create/patch responses (`warning` field), and the task drawer computed `humanGuideWarning` with `data-test-id="human-guide-warning"`.

`HUMAN_TASK_SCAFFOLD` and the human split template in `src/core/human-step-tags.ts` both include `## Step-by-step guide` plus a short italic prompt describing what to write. That satisfies the `--human` scaffold acceptance criterion and ensures `repoos split` / PM-driven human splits do not create guideless bodies. Engineer default instructions in `src/core/config.ts` now require a complete guide when asking for a human split; the PM default instructions require the section for any `--assigned-to human` task and explicitly exempt AI tasks.

Warnings are advisory: creation and update still succeed. This matches the spec (existing tasks are not rewritten or blocked) and mirrors how underspecified detection works for agent tasks — visibility first, coercion through agent instructions second.

## Approaches tried

The task spec suggested making the warning the primary enforcement because per-project `repoos.toml` agent overrides will not automatically inherit built-in prompt edits. The implementation follows that split: **prompts guide**, **`humanTaskGuideWarning` warns everywhere humans and tooling look**.

Heading detection uses a line-anchored regex (`^## Step-by-step guide\s*$` with `im` flags) rather than parsing the full section tree. That keeps the check cheap and aligned with how other task sections are recognized elsewhere in the repo. A heading with only placeholder text under it counts as present — appropriate for freshly scaffolded human tasks that still need flesh on the steps.

UI placement reuses the existing `hotfix-banner` pattern above the drawer tabs so the warning is visible without opening the markdown editor, consistent with other task-level notices.

## Challenges and blockers

The prior managed turn ended with a network timeout (`read ETIMEDOUT`) before handoff; no code was missing on resume. The branch already contained the feature commits (checkpointed WIP commits from self-check). Resume work was validation: re-run `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` (passed after ~12 minutes including queued gate), confirm shots declaration on the task file, and author this engineering report.

No product decisions were blocked. The acceptance criterion that `repoos update --section "Step-by-step guide" --section-body ...` works relies on the generic section patch path already used for other headings; tests in `cli-task-flags-help.test.ts` exercise human scaffold output and CLI warning text.

## Key learnings

Human tasks are a different reader contract than agent tasks. Reusing agent-oriented stubs (`needs-human-step`, underspecified heuristics) was already gated for `assignee: human` (#0815); this change adds the positive requirement humans actually need — operable steps — without dragging AI-only sections like `## Notes for AI` into human checklists.

Keeping warning text in one exported function avoids CLI/API/UI drift. Any future tweak to wording or detection (e.g. requiring non-empty guide content, not just the heading) should stay in `humanTaskGuideWarning` with table-driven tests in `task-underspecified-flag.test.ts` and CLI integration tests.

The declared review shot (`card:humanStep` fixture, highlight on `human-guide-warning`) gives reviewers a deterministic place to see the banner when a human task omits the section; auto UI shots from the diff should also pick up `TaskDrawer.vue` changes.
